method: Independent lens review of captured evidence. The director opened every screenshot for a surface before scoring it, read the axe and capture results, and scored without sight of any other director's scores.
overallNote: Signal Studio's text contrast is genuinely better than most shipping products: the lowest value I measured anywhere across fourteen captures was 4.63:1, most body text sits between 7.7:1 and 10.4:1, and status is never encoded by color alone — every colored dot, chip and rail icon is paired with a visible text label. That is deliberate, systemic work and it should be said plainly. The failures are concentrated in two places. First, non-text contrast: this design system draws its boundaries and states at 1.06:1 to 1.38:1 — card borders 1.36:1, the landing page's secondary CTA border 1.24:1, and the Timeline/Milestones selected state at a 1.06:1 fill difference, which is a measurable 1.4.11 failure on a control that tells the user which view they are in. Second, target size: the task complete-toggle renders at 16x16 CSS px on every view and every viewport, and list rows place two 16px targets 30px apart, clearing SC 2.5.8's spacing exception by six pixels. Both are cheap to fix and neither is visible to axe. I have not vetoed anything: no single defect here would embarrass the company or hard-block a user outright. But I want the thinness of the automated signal recorded. Sixteen page-states returned empty violations arrays with no ruleset, no passes and no incomplete counts, and zero violations is not zero barriers. Nothing is focused in any capture, so focus visibility — the thing most at risk in a system whose hairlines run at 1.24:1 — is entirely unevidenced. Board drag-and-drop keyboard operation, modal focus trap and return-focus, list-view grid semantics, live-region announcement and 320px/200%-zoom reflow are all unverified. And the app advertises bare single-character shortcuts (c, e, j, k, /) with no visible remap or disable, which is a probable WCAG 2.1.4 Level A failure that no automated pass will ever surface. Scores reflect what the evidence supports, not what the product may well do correctly once exercised with a keyboard and a screen reader.

surfaces.rationale: Measured text contrast is excellent (column descriptions 7.73:1, 'Day 11 of 97' 5.60:1, '1 overdue' chip 5.47:1) and no status is color-alone — every dot is paired with a text label ('To do', 'In progress', 'High'). But the interactive layer is weak. The complete-toggle circle measures 16x16 CSS px on board and list, desktop and mobile; list rows stack a 16px square select box and a 16px circle toggle 30px apart in a 38px row, which clears SC 2.5.8's spacing exception by 6px and is genuinely hard for anyone with a tremor — and a misfire toggles completion. Card boundaries sit at 1.36:1 and the 'To do' hollow ring at 1.38:1, the amber 'In progress' dot at 2.15:1, all under the 3:1 of 1.4.11. The desktop list clips its Priority column at 1440px — 'Hig', 'Low', 'No' cut mid-word against the viewport edge — so content is lost at a mainstream desktop width, not just under zoom. Mobile board is a horizontal carousel clipping 'Mara & F' and 'Menu ta' mid-word. Keyboard operation of column drag-and-drop, the classic Kanban trap, is entirely unevidenced by static captures, as is any focus indicator. The persistent 'In development' toast covers two Done rows in the list capture.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Raise the complete-toggle to a 24x24 minimum hit area (keeping the 16px visual if desired) and prove a visible focus ring plus a keyboard path for moving a task between columns — the board's densest, most-used control is currently both the smallest and the least verifiable.

surfaces.rationale: The modal reads as considered work: 'Mark done' is a filled indigo button with a real text label at 6.29:1, section labels and placeholders sit at 4.83:1, the header control cluster (prev, next, expand, overflow, close) is spaced 36px apart on desktop and 48px on mobile so the spacing exception is comfortably met, and mobile reflow to a single column with metadata relocated below the conversation is clean and correct. Two things hold it down. First, the surface actively advertises single-character shortcuts — 'Press e to open a task full-screen, and j or k to move between tasks', alongside the 'C' badge for Add task — with no visible remap or disable affordance; that is a probable WCAG 2.1.4 Level A failure and a real hazard for speech-input users, and axe cannot see it. Second, this is the one surface where focus trapping, initial focus placement, return-focus to the originating card, aria-modal and the accessible names of the five icon-only header buttons decide whether it works at all, and a static capture shows none of it. The mobile close glyph measures 8x8px. The dropzone border at 3.38:1 passes but only just.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Add a settings-level mechanism to disable or remap the single-key shortcuts (e/j/k/c//), or scope them to focus, and evidence the dialog's focus trap and return-focus — the modal advertises a keyboard model it has not shown it honours accessibly.

surfaces.rationale: The strongest app surface through this lens. Actions are real text buttons at generous size — 'Keep', 'Turn into task', 'Delete' — rather than icon guesswork, with Delete at 6.09:1 red on white. The selected note is encoded three ways at once (indigo left bar at 6.29:1, tinted fill, position), which is exactly the redundancy low-vision users need. Chips carry text plus color ('In Tasks' 4.82:1, 'To review' 5.39:1), composer and search placeholders hit 7.73:1, and the reader's task link runs 6.37:1. Three real gaps. The note-type indicator in the list — written, voice, photo — is an icon with no visible text equivalent, so type is conveyed graphically only in the list (the reader spells out 'Written', the list does not). On mobile the 'In development' toast lands directly on top of the Keep / Turn into task / Delete row, obscuring three interactive controls; that is the clearest content-obscuring defect in the whole evidence set. The '/' search shortcut is another bare single-key binding. The active 'Notebook' tab's fill bleeds to x=0 with no inset on mobile.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Move the persistent 'In development' toast out of the interaction layer (inset it above the bottom nav, or make it dismissible-once) so it stops covering the Keep / Turn into task / Delete controls on mobile.

surfaces.rationale: The milestone graphics are better than expected: future hollow rings measure 6.72–7.15:1 and the axis 19:1, all far above the 3:1 of 1.4.11, and milestone state is carried by text eyebrows — 'Complete', 'Coming up', 'Our next milestone', 'Later' — not by color alone. That is deliberate work. Two defects pull it down. The Timeline/Milestones segmented control signals its selected state with a white fill against a #f4f4f5 sibling — a 1.06:1 difference — plus a 1.28:1 border; a scan through the control at y=108 confirms no other distinguishing affordance, so which view is current is effectively imperceptible, a measurable 1.4.11 state-contrast failure. Separately, the five clustered dots at the right of the axis carry no text label at all, only a '4 milestones' bracket, so those milestones' identity is positional and graphic only. The dots measure roughly 10px; whether they are interactive, and what hit area they carry, cannot be determined from a static capture. For a sharing surface, the consequential privacy state — 'Live since 15 Jul 2026. Anyone holding the link can read it.' — is set in 13px gray at 7.73:1, correct in contrast but very quiet for what it discloses.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Give the Timeline/Milestones control a selected state that clears 3:1 against its unselected sibling (fill, weight, or an underline bar) — the current 1.06:1 fill difference leaves the active view unreadable to anyone with reduced contrast sensitivity.

surfaces.rationale: Contrast is handled well: nav items at 4.83:1, the violet 'outside' at 6.29:1 in a ~92px hero (needs only 3:1 at that size), subcopy at 10.44:1, the black primary button at 18.88:1, and the 'NOTES to TASKS to TIMELINE' monospace line at 5.84:1 despite its small size. A single H1, sensible reading order, and a mobile layout that stacks both CTAs full-width with generous targets and a 24px hamburger. The concrete defect is the 'Join the waitlist' secondary button: its label is plain dark text on white and its only affordance is a border measuring 1.24:1, so the boundary that identifies it as a control is invisible to low-vision users — and this is a primary conversion action sitting beside the filled black button. Beyond that, nothing is focused in either capture so focus visibility on the nav and CTAs is unevidenced, and the 'Products' disclosure's expanded/collapsed semantics and the hamburger's accessible name cannot be confirmed from pixels.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Raise the 'Join the waitlist' button border to at least 3:1 against white (or give it a fill) — at 1.24:1 the page's secondary CTA is not perceivable as a control.

surfaces.rationale: Through this lens there is very little to hold against it. Body copy measures 10.01:1 on the off-white ground and the 'A NOTE FROM THE FOUNDER' eyebrow 10.81:1 despite being small uppercase; the measure is comfortable, there is a single clear H1, and the mobile capture reflows to one column with type scaling sensibly and no clipping or horizontal overflow. The page carries almost no interactive surface of its own, which removes most of the target-size and state-contrast risk that drags the app surfaces down. What keeps it below the 9.5 floor is not a visible defect but unevidenced behaviour: no element is focused in either capture, so focus-ring visibility across the shared nav is unproven, and given this design system's hairlines run at 1.24–1.66:1 that is a live risk rather than an idle one. The shared header's 'Products' disclosure semantics and the icon-only mobile hamburger's accessible name are likewise unverifiable. The decorative indigo left rule at 1.66:1 carries no information, so it is correctly exempt.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Evidence a visible focus indicator meeting 3:1 on the shared header nav, disclosure and hamburger — the page's own content is clean, so the remaining risk is entirely in the chrome it inherits.

surfaces.rationale: What the capture shows is well handled: the 'PRICING' eyebrow at 6.29:1 even at ~11px monospace, hero subcopy at 10.44:1, fact labels at 18.09:1 with their subtext at 4.63:1, and a three-fact strip whose vertical dividers (1.24:1, decorative) become horizontal rules when it stacks cleanly on mobile with no overflow. But the evidence has a hole in exactly the place this lens most needs to look: both captures stop at the 'Choose by the work in front of you' heading, before any plan card, tier comparison, or billing-period control appears. The accessibility-critical content of a pricing page — whether the comparison is a real table with header associations, whether plan selection is a proper radio group, whether a monthly/annual toggle announces its state, whether price and period are programmatically associated — is entirely absent, and axe reporting an empty violations array for a viewport that never reached the tiers is not evidence they are sound. I am scoring what is visible as good and discounting heavily rather than extending optimism to an unevaluable core.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Re-capture the page at full scroll length so the plan cards, comparison table and any billing toggle can actually be assessed for table semantics, selection-control roles and state announcement — the current evidence cannot support a release judgement on this surface.
